channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated reading: AI & geopolitics, chips, film & streaming, South African rugby

item.title: The monster Chris Hansen sees in Primetime, explained
item.description: Film analysis of the 'monster' motif in Primetime, the Chris Hansen / To Catch a Predator drama. Argues the creature reflects Hansen's own moral certainty and ratings desperation, and reads the film as a parallel to post-9/11 'with us or against us' thinking.

item.title: Designing Friction
item.description: A design manifesto arguing digital products should build in resistance, delay and discomfort as a counterweight to frictionless, algorithm-driven UX, in order to preserve human autonomy and deeper engagement.

item.title: How are countries evaluating AI models?
item.description: Brookings Institution analysis of how different governments approach testing and assessing AI models, and what the differing methods mean for international cooperation on AI governance.

item.title: Feeding the beast: Energy security as a precondition for the EU's AI power
item.description: Policy brief on how electricity access shapes the global AI race, covering Europe's energy costs, grid limits and import dependence, and how data centre siting might turn these constraints into a strength.

item.title: The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit
item.description: Survey of competing international AI governance efforts, including Chinese and US-led initiatives, UN processes and the EU AI Act, with recommendations for US policymakers ahead of bilateral talks.

item.title: TSMC, ASML eye 12-inch photomasks to unlock High-NA EUV's full-field potential
item.description: Report on TSMC and ASML exploring larger photomasks as a route to full-field High-NA EUV lithography for 2nm and angstrom-era nodes. The full text is paywalled.

item.title: Can a Radioactive Ore Break China's Grip on Rare Earths?
item.description: Looks at monazite as a possible source of rare earths outside China, weighing thorium waste handling, regulatory hurdles and the speculative dealmaking that has dogged the sector.

item.title: Why Everyone Is Talking About Hybrid Bonding, and Who Is in the Race
item.description: Explainer on hybrid bonding in advanced packaging, covering bonding methods, bottlenecks and the main suppliers as chip stacking and chiplets spread. Only part is free to read.

item.title: Bela Bajaria Was Fired Wednesday. Next Week Netflix Faces Wall Street
item.description: Reports on Netflix's content-chief change and roughly 1,000 job cuts, set against a weak stock year and expectations for the upcoming quarterly results. The article is partly paywalled.

item.title: Digger is Tom Cruise's worst box-office opening in 20 years, can lose $150 million
item.description: Breaks down the weak opening of Digger against its reported budget and marketing spend, and estimates how large the studio's eventual loss could be.

item.title: Disney Is Opening the Door to Netflix—and Changing the Streaming Playbook
item.description: Examines Disney's decision to license catalog titles to Netflix, tying it to falling linear TV revenue and debt, and compares the two companies' financials and valuations.

item.title: Bulls player ratings vs Stade Francais | 2026/27 Investec Champions Cup
item.description: Individual player ratings for the Bulls after their 56-20 Champions Cup opener at Loftus on 17 October.

item.title: Stormers thump Bristol despite first-half red card
item.description: Match report on the Stormers' 49-12 Champions Cup win over Bristol in Cape Town, achieved with a player sent off in the first half.

item.title: Springboks: Frans Malherbe issues 'hopeful' update after 19-month-long absence
item.description: Update on the Springbok prop's recovery, noting he has returned to non-contact team training with no decision yet on his future.

item.title: US-China race is on for the Gulf's AI future
item.description: An analysis of how Washington and Beijing compete to supply AI and digital infrastructure to Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and how Gulf states hedge between them. It considers the effect of the regional conflict on trust in US security guarantees.

item.title: Key watchdogs signal they will step up AI regulation
item.description: Looks at financial regulators and the UK moving toward closer oversight of AI models, set against a US administration with little appetite for tougher rules. Also touches on how China's approach to AI safety is characterised.

item.title: Why data centers are a top issue in the 2026 midterms
item.description: Commentary on why data center buildouts have become a campaign issue in both parties, tied to electricity prices, water use and wider affordability worries. Considers what the midterm results could mean for future AI infrastructure policy and investment.

item.title: What ASML Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
item.description: Summary of ASML's third-quarter results and outlook, covering EUV output plans, whether supply can keep up with AI-driven demand through 2028, and where High-NA adoption stands among its main customers.

item.title: Hot Chips 2026: Micron warns HBM wafer penalty is widening with every generation
item.description: Covers a Micron talk on how much more wafer area high-bandwidth memory consumes than standard DRAM and why that gap is growing. Connects it to memory pricing and supply tightness.

item.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
item.description: Weekly roundup spanning a packaging interposer deal between TSMC and GlobalFoundries, silicon carbide funding, nanoimprint and hyper-NA lithography developments, and industry sales and policy news.

item.title: How the Streamers Stack Up in Subscribers, Revenue and Profits
item.description: Side-by-side comparison of the major studios' streaming businesses using their latest quarterly figures for revenue, profit and subscribers. Also notes the status of the pending Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger.

item.title: Box Office Is Back. Now Comes the War Over Who Gets the Upside
item.description: Explains how talent profit participation, studio fees and streaming bonuses work as theatrical revenue recovers. Uses a low-budget hit as a case study in who gets paid when a film succeeds.

item.title: Netflix Is Out-Lobbying All of Hollywood
item.description: Data-driven look at 27 years of federal lobbying filings by the film industry, finding Netflix now outspends the MPA in Washington. Examines what each is lobbying for.

item.title: Stormers 49-12 Bristol Bears: Likely lads give Pat Lam's young side a lesson in finishing
item.description: Match report on the Stormers' bonus-point Champions Cup win over a young Bristol side in Cape Town, the most recent Stormers match. Notes Bristol's promise and their defensive lapses.

item.title: Lions' bravery in France speaks louder than Champions Cup defeat after Hyron Andrews' death
item.description: Opinion piece on the Lions' Champions Cup debut against La Rochelle, played after the death of lock Hyron Andrews, and the team's response on the day.

item.title: State of the URC: Wounded locals await Sharks, Lions
item.description: Early-season check on the four South African URC sides after round two, with the standings picture and a look ahead to the first local derbies.
